examples.en: This coffee is too bitter. Do you have sugar?

examples.ko: 이 약은 입에 쓰지만 꼭 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: This medicine tastes bitter, but you must take it.
If you don't add sugar, it tastes bitter.

examples.ko: 너무 쓰면 우유를 조금 넣어 보세요.
examples.en: If it's too bitter, try adding a little milk.
My mouth tastes bitter, so I can't eat.

examples.ko: 이 채소는 맛이 좀 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This vegetable can taste a bit bitter.

explain: 맛을 말하는 '쓰다'는 형용사라서 '써요, 써서'처럼 '아/어' 앞에서 '으'가 빠지고, 꾸밀 때는 '쓴 커피'가 돼요. 반대말은 '달다'예요. 글을 쓰다·모자를 쓰다는 동사라서 '쓰는 사람'처럼 '는'이 붙어요.

phrases.en: I got a bitter taste of failure when my first business failed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실패나 어려움을 직접 겪고 힘들었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means going through failure or hardship yourself and finding it painful.
phrases.en_equiv: to get a taste of hardship

explain_en: As a taste word it is an adjective. The '으' drops before '아/어', as in 써요 and 써서, and it becomes '쓴 커피' when modifying a noun. Its opposite is '달다' (sweet). The verbs for writing and wearing take '는', as in '쓰는 사람'.

examples.en: It's cold outside, so I wear a hat.
My eyesight is bad, so I go around wearing glasses.
It's a little hard to breathe when I wear a mask.
The sun is strong today, so wear sunglasses.

examples.ko: 자전거를 탈 때는 헬멧을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear a helmet when riding a bike.

examples.ko: 어제 제가 쓴 모자 못 봤어요?
examples.en: Did you see the hat I wore yesterday?

explain: 모자, 안경, 마스크, 선글라스처럼 머리나 얼굴에 올리는 것에 써요. 옷은 '입다', 신발은 '신다', 시계는 '차다', 반지는 '끼다'를 써요. 우산을 쓰다(use an umbrella)도 같은 '쓰다'예요. 벗을 때는 '벗다'를 써요.

phrases.en: My eyesight is bad, so I wear glasses.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for putting on or wearing glasses.

explain_en: Use it for things you put on your head or face, such as hats, glasses, masks and sunglasses. Clothes use '입다', shoes use '신다', watches use '차다' and rings use '끼다'. Putting up an umbrella is also '쓰다', and taking things off is '벗다'.

examples.en: Try taking a deep breath.
Breathing through the nose is comfortable.
It's hard to breathe because of my cold.
The baby sleeps, breathing quietly.

examples.ko: 갑자기 숨을 쉴 수 없어서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was scared because I suddenly couldn't breathe.
After exercising, I took a big breath.

explain: 거의 항상 '숨을 쉬다'로 써요. 한숨이면 '한숨을 쉬다'라고 해요. 휴식의 '쉬다'와 모양과 활용이 같아서('쉬어요') '숨'이 있으면 호흡이에요. 병원이나 설명하는 글에서는 '호흡하다'도 써요.

phrases.example: 요즘 일이 너무 많아서 숨 쉴 틈이 없어요.
phrases.en: I have so much work lately that I don't have a moment to breathe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 바빠서 잠깐 쉴 시간도 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means you are so busy that you do not even have a moment to rest.
phrases.en_equiv: no time to catch one's breath

explain_en: It is almost always used as '숨을 쉬다'. For a sigh, you say '한숨을 쉬다'. It looks and conjugates the same as '쉬다' (to rest), as in 쉬어요, so the word '숨' tells you it means breathing. In hospitals and explanatory writing, '호흡하다' is also used.

examples.en: The seeds of this apple are very small.
When spring comes, we sow seeds in the field.
When you eat watermelon, spit out the seeds.

examples.ko: 이 과일은 씨도 많고 껍질도 두꺼워요.
examples.en: This fruit has many seeds and a thick skin.

examples.ko: 씨 몇 개를 화분에 심어 보세요.
examples.en: Try planting a few seeds in a flowerpot.
I was eating grapes and ended up swallowing the seeds too.

explain: '씨'는 과일 속에 든 것에도, 심으려고 모은 것에도 써요. 심는 것을 가리킬 때는 '씨앗'이 더 자연스러워요. '수박씨, 호박씨'처럼 앞말에 붙여 써요. 이름 뒤에 붙는 '씨'(Mr./Ms.)와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 인기 있는 인형이라 가게마다 씨가 말랐어요.
phrases.en: It's a popular doll, so every shop has run out completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것이 하나도 남지 않을 만큼 완전히 없어졌다는 뜻이에요. '마르다'가 '말랐어요'로 활용돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means something has disappeared so completely that none is left. '마르다' conjugates as '말랐어요'.

explain_en: '씨' is used both for the seeds inside fruit and for seeds gathered for planting. When you mean seeds to plant, '씨앗' sounds more natural. It attaches to the preceding word, as in '수박씨' and '호박씨'. It is a different word from '씨' (Mr./Ms.) after a name.
